# one-by.one — factual product and policy overview

Coming soon to iPhone. English-only product for users aged 16 and over. This overview summarizes product facts and the English legal pages dated October 5, 2026. The privacy policy and terms contain the full legal wording.

## Launch scope and language
Last updated: October 5, 2026. Worldwide launch except the entire EU/EEA (the 27 EU member states: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain and Sweden; plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway), the United Kingdom, Switzerland, mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao (Macau), Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Türkiye (Turkey) and Vietnam. These exclusions reflect representative requirements in the EU/EEA, United Kingdom and Switzerland, and ChatGPT/Claude availability, sanctions, registration or localization requirements in the other excluded markets. The interface is English-only; App Store availability and prices are country-specific. See https://one-by.one/terms/#launch-scope.

## Product and workflow
one-by.one is the execution layer for the AI you already use. Your AI plans the whole day; the iPhone app delivers action cards, keeps running and waiting work, and records results. Starter sets are fixed card sets for use without an AI connection. one-by.one does not itself call an AI model. Start, Done, Not today and Undo handle execution.

One card is one doable action. Long tasks, workout sets, recipe steps and rests are split into separate ordered cards. Pomodoro and doing something else while waiting are planning patterns made from ordinary cards. The server is the source of truth for plans and records.

Results can be recorded with units: weight, repetitions, distance, duration, volume, energy, nutrients, pages, cups, cigarettes or games. Things already done can be saved as past results. AI-estimated values, such as nutrition estimated from a meal description, must be labelled estimated. Records shows today and week totals. Share images are generated on the device; one-by.one does not upload them as part of rendering. A selected recipient or app receives an image only when you share it, under that recipient’s policies.

Interests hold ongoing practices, such as guitar, and recurring duties as plain schedule lines, such as “Mondays: ...” or “Last day of month: ...”. Saved context, memories, corrections and retained originals can be included in tool replies. Reads may be limited or paginated and do not establish a complete lifetime history.

## AI connection and changes
The custom MCP connector address is https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp. The setup guide is https://one-by.one/connect/ (Korean: https://one-by.one/ko/connect/). Any remote HTTP MCP agent with OAuth discovery and dynamic client registration can connect. Local loopback redirects are supported. Up to three AI connections are allowed per account. Unverified clients are labelled Unverified app on the approval screen. The authorization web is https://connect.one-by.one. Sign in with Apple or Google and follow Settings › AI apps. Email sign-in is for existing accounts; email account creation is not offered. When a directory listing becomes available, search for one-by.one in the AI service’s apps or connectors directory. A listing is not assumed to be available now.

OAuth authenticates identity. Separate product approvals are recorded on the consent page: context:read, activity:read and activity:write. These control planning context, activity reads and changes. The AI can plan days, edit unstarted cards, save interests and memories, and record or correct results within approved permissions.

Starting work, undoing an eligible mistaken start before any later record, taking a card off today, fixing or withdrawing recorded times, and completing a task require the user’s explicit request. Time correction does not control execution. Some changes cannot be undone, and corrections can preserve originals. The server checks granted permissions but cannot prove what the user agreed to in chat.

Personal assistants are a core audience. MCP capability, OAuth support and the AI service’s own connector access requirements determine whether a client can connect. This overview does not confirm individual compatibility with ChatGPT Dots, Meta Muse or Grok Bot. ChatGPT and Claude are separate services with their own terms and privacy settings; review those before connecting.

## Subscription, trial and cancellation
one-by.one offers monthly and annual auto-renewing subscriptions through the App Store. Apple’s purchase confirmation shows the price, billing period, eligible introductory offers and renewal terms. Manage or cancel renewal in Apple Account settings. Deleting the app or account, signing out or declining consent does not cancel a subscription.

## Privacy stance
No sale of data, advertising use or cross-app tracking. Text entered into plans, tasks, memories or reports may contain sensitive information; share only what you want stored and available to a connected AI. AI provider policies and settings govern chats and tool data they receive.

The following sections reproduce the current English privacy wording as readable text.

This policy covers the one-by.one website, iPhone app and MCP connection service, operated by salad76, a sole proprietorship in the Republic of Korea represented by Seungeun Kim, doing business as one-by.one. one-by.one is an execution layer for the AI service you already use. Your connected AI prepares plans; one-by.one presents their actions as cards and keeps execution records that the AI can read with your permission. one-by.one does not itself call an AI model.

Starter sets are fixed card sets supplied in the app, not AI-generated plans. Creating cards from these sets happens on your device and does not send data outside it.

The launch scope is worldwide except the countries and territories listed in our terms. The interface is English-only.

## Launch waitlist

If you ask to be notified at launch, we store your email address, signup time and signup page, plus an email hash to prevent duplicate signups. We use this to send one launch email, with no further marketing unless you opt in later. We also use a hashed IP address to limit abusive submissions; these rate-limit records become eligible for cleanup after two days of inactivity.

Waitlist entries become eligible for cleanup 30 days after the launch notice, or when unsubscribed. To remove your signup before then, email privacy@one-by.one.

## What we collect

- Account: account ID, email when available, provider identity and sessions, to sign you in and link your records. Apple sign-in requests email. Google sign-in requests openid email profile. Google identity and access tokens are sent to Supabase Auth for sign-in. The app keeps its session in device-only Keychain storage; web authorization uses browser session storage.

- Plans and results: full task titles, notes, steps, dates, time zones, estimates, targets, measurements, progress, execution records, corrections and versions. These show your day plan and what to do now, record results and support synchronization.

- Interests and memories: titles, planning notes, memory text, user reports, AI summaries and inferences, sources and timestamps. These provide saved planning context. Corrections and withdrawals retain originals.

- Connections and operation: device and AI connection IDs, credential references, hashed server credentials, permissions, approvals, expiry, revocation, synchronization records, write requests and receipts, request-limit records and local startup/sign-in diagnostics. These control access and support retries and operation. To limit abusive subscription-linking requests, we store a SHA-256 hash derived from the request’s IP address, a rate-limit window timestamp and an attempt count. This rate-limit table does not store the raw IP address. Network providers may separately process IP addresses to deliver and protect requests.

- Support: messages you email us and account-linked bug descriptions, submission IDs, hashes, received times and selected app version, iOS version or error code. Bug-report tools add no automatic attachments.

- Subscription: Apple handles payments. We receive and store subscription product and transaction identifiers, purchase-to-account associations, purchase claim tokens, verification status, environment, and relevant purchase, expiry and grace-period dates. These records let us verify access and link an eligible purchase made before sign-in to a one-by.one account. We do not receive your payment-card details.

- Deletion processing: Account deletion can leave a limited deletion receipt containing the deletion request identifier, hashes of the account identifier and recovery capability, and Apple revocation status and job reference. An Apple revocation job can retain encrypted authorization material and the Apple account subject needed to retry revocation, together with retry and status metadata. These records are described under Retention.

If you sign in with Google, our sign-in provider stores what Google shares for that sign-in: your email address and whether Google verified it, your name, your profile picture link and your Google account identifier.

Text you enter may contain health, work, location or other sensitive details. Share only what you want stored and available to your connected AI.

The app can schedule local reminders for running timed cards. Delivery depends on your notification settings, quiet hours and the state last known to this iPhone. The current app does not register for remote push.

For App Store subscription prices, introductory offers and renewal terms, see our terms and Apple’s purchase confirmation.

## Purposes and grounds for processing

- Account, synchronization and AI connections: we process account identity, sessions, saved plans, results, interests, memories and approved connection permissions as needed to provide the service you request. AI access is limited to the permissions you approve; connecting an AI is optional. Storage consent and the separate optional AI and calendar choices are described below.

- Subscription verification: we process transaction references and entitlement status to provide paid access and meet applicable purchase-record obligations. Apple handles payment details.

- Support and privacy requests: we use the messages and diagnostics you choose to send to answer your request; we process privacy requests to meet applicable legal obligations. Please avoid including health or other sensitive information that is unnecessary for your request.

- Security and service operation: we use access, request-limit and technical records as needed to protect accounts, prevent abuse and operate the service, subject to applicable law and any consent it requires.

- Launch waitlist: your voluntary signup authorizes one launch email. You can withdraw by unsubscribing or emailing us; rate-limit records are used only to prevent abusive submissions.

Saving and syncing records is a condition of using one-by.one’s recording and execution features. Records can include meals, exercise, quantities and other health-related information. The current service requires storage consent for record changes and for connected AI apps to read account records; it does not offer a separate non-health recording mode.

You may decline or withdraw storage consent. New record changes and uploads are then blocked, and connected AI apps cannot read your records. Existing records are not deleted by withdrawal. Declining during initial setup stops setup; you can go back, sign out and manage an existing Apple subscription. For access to your data, a portable copy or account deletion assistance, contact privacy@one-by.one.

Connecting an AI app and sharing calendar data are separate, optional choices. Storage consent alone does not authorize an AI connection. Declining or withdrawing consent does not cancel an Apple subscription.

## Consumer health data and explicit consent

Meal and intake records, exercise or fitness activity, weight, medication and other health-related measurements, notes, results or AI inferences may reveal physical or mental health. We treat these as sensitive health-related data. They come from information or measurements you choose to record and from your approved AI's reports or inferences based on that content.

We use this data only to save your requested records, synchronize them, show progress and provide the planning or changes you request. Supabase hosts and processes it; Cloudflare carries authorized AI requests and replies; your chosen AI provider receives it when you separately consent to sharing and approve the relevant connection permissions. These are the recipients and categories of recipients for these uses. If you put health information in a support email, our email provider also receives it as described under International transfers.

Saving and syncing health-related records is subject to the storage consent condition above. Each AI connection and calendar sharing require separate approval.

You can withdraw storage consent in the app's Settings or email privacy@one-by.one. Withdrawal stops future collection or sharing covered by that consent when the service receives and confirms the request; an offline request must reconnect to reach the server. Withdrawal does not itself delete existing records or copies already received by an AI provider. You can separately request deletion, including retained originals and history, using the rights procedure below. Withdrawal does not affect processing already lawfully carried out.

We do not sell consumer health data or use it for targeted advertising. Washington's My Health My Data Act and Nevada's SB 370 provide consumer health-data protections that may apply even when other state privacy laws do not. See Major regional privacy rights for access, withdrawal, deletion and appeal options.

## Calendar (optional)

Calendar sharing is optional and off until you consent and choose calendars. You can withdraw in Settings by turning off calendar sharing, or email privacy@one-by.one for help.

If you enable calendar sharing and choose calendars, one-by.one uploads a snapshot covering the next seven days. It contains event titles, start and end times, all-day status, tentative status where available, hashed event and calendar identifiers, and snapshot metadata such as capture time, time zone, coverage dates and whether the snapshot is incomplete.

On your iPhone, calendar access also reads calendar identifiers and names, event metadata and your attendance or availability status to select the events to share. Event locations can be read by the local calendar reader but are excluded from the uploaded snapshot. Calendar notes, attendee details, locations and URLs are not uploaded. one-by.one does not edit your calendar events.

With Share times only enabled, uploaded event titles are replaced with “Busy.” Previously uploaded titles are removed when the server confirms withdrawal of the earlier snapshot. Information already received by an AI provider is not automatically removed.

We keep only the latest uploaded calendar snapshot for your account and refresh it when you return to the app, at most once every 15 minutes unless you change your calendar selection or the times-only option.

Calendar data remains available to connected AI until the server confirms withdrawal. Offline withdrawal is retried when the app reconnects. Deleting your account also deletes its uploaded calendar snapshot.

## What your AI app receives

When an AI connection you have approved calls an MCP tool, one-by.one returns the account data allowed by that connection’s permissions. Depending on the request, this can include saved interests and planning notes; plans and action cards; running, waiting and completed activity; targets, quantities and recorded results; corrections and retained originals; saved memories and their sources; and calendar snapshots you separately chose to share. Replies can also contain identifiers, versions, access permissions, write handles and operation receipts.

Each connection requires its own approval. context:read allows relevant planning context, activity:read allows activity records, and activity:write allows supported changes. The approval page shows the requested access. MCP tool replies do not expose sign-in credentials, provider tokens or device secrets. User-written content can itself contain identifying or sensitive information.

ChatGPT, Claude and other connected AI services are operated by their respective providers. Their policies, account type and settings govern the copies they receive, including retention and any use to improve their services. one-by.one does not control those independent copies. Disconnecting stops future access through that connection; it does not automatically delete previously received information.

OAuth account-information requests are separate from MCP record replies. Review the OAuth scopes displayed on the approval screen.

Write instructions require your explicit request. The server checks granted permissions but cannot prove what you agreed to in chat. Some changes cannot be undone; corrections can preserve originals.

What connected tools can do

Available tools vary with the account and supported features. They can read planning context and records, create or change plans, record requested execution changes and results, manage saved interests and memories, and submit an approved support report. A tool response can be paginated or incomplete and is not necessarily a complete lifetime history.

Read plans and tasks

get_planning_context, list_current_work, get_current_work: read planning context, task lists and task/result records.

Plan days and edit unstarted tasks

open_or_plan_day, edit_day_plan, replace_plan: open or plan days, change queued cards and replace unstarted plans.

Start and correct work

start_work, undo_start, correct_work_time: start a task, undo an eligible mistaken start, or amend or withdraw a recorded time while retaining its original. Time correction does not control execution.

Save and correct results

record_past_result, correct_recorded_result, complete_work: record separate past work, correct or withdraw a result's interpretation, or mark work complete.

Read interests and memories

list_interests, get_interest: read saved interests, context and memories, including retained originals.

Save and change interests and memories

create_interest, replace_interest_context, save_interest_memory, correct_interest_memory: save interests and memories, replace context or correct or withdraw a memory while retaining its original.

Connection and support

get_connection_info: read permissions and supported features, and receive a write token when available. submit_bug_report: send an approved report to one-by.one support and receive a receipt.

## Prompt links and clipboard

When you choose Copy and open, one-by.one copies the displayed prompt to the system clipboard and opens the selected AI service. For ChatGPT and Claude, the prompt is also included in the opening URL. Opening that URL can disclose the prompt to the service before you press Send in the chat. Prompts can contain the onboarding answers and planning details used to prepare them.

Copy only places the text on the clipboard without opening an AI link. Other apps receive it if you paste or otherwise share it through your device’s clipboard features. Gemini currently opens without a prompt in its URL, while the text remains available on the clipboard. These actions are separate from approving access to saved records through MCP.

## Sharing images

Share images are generated on your device. one-by.one does not upload the generated image as part of rendering it. If you share it, the app or recipient you select receives that image under its own policies. Review the final image before sharing. Automatic keyword warnings or exclusions cannot identify every sensitive item.

## Operator access and encryption

We don't routinely look at your content. Operator access to stored data is limited to fixing a problem you report, keeping the service secure, or meeting a legal obligation. Access to account records is checked against account ownership and approved permissions. The service processes readable content to provide synchronization and authorized tool replies; it does not provide end-to-end encryption that prevents the service from reading that content. App sessions are stored in device-only Keychain storage.

## Storage and providers

- Supabase: account identity, sessions, product content, reports and server processing. Production server data is hosted in the United States (Supabase US). The service processes content for your requested features, protected by account access restrictions.

- Cloudflare: the MCP proxy carries authorized requests and replies between the AI client and Supabase.

- Apple: sign-in, App Store subscriptions and device services.

- Google: Google sign-in and identity tokens passed to Supabase Auth.

- Your chosen AI client: the requests and replies described above.

- Support and privacy email: Cloudflare Inc. routes messages sent to support@one-by.one and privacy@one-by.one through Cloudflare Email Routing to Google LLC (Gmail), which stores the mailbox. Processing takes place in the United States and other countries where these providers operate data centers.

These providers process data to operate their services. Their own policies apply to their handling. Data may be processed outside your country of residence.

The iPhone keeps local records and credentials. The current app does not automatically sync its local database through CloudKit and does not upload private CloudKit backups.

## International transfers

The following describes the recipients, data, purposes and transfer choices for the service. Transfers occur through encrypted network connections when you use the corresponding feature. Provider contact and privacy information is linked below; you can also contact privacy@one-by.one about your rights.

Supabase Inc. — United States — hosting and database

Account identifiers, sign-in sessions, plans, results, interests, selected calendar snapshots, connection permissions, subscription metadata and support reports are transferred when you sign in, synchronize records or submit a report, for hosting, database processing and access verification. Account content is retained while your account exists; record-specific cleanup eligibility and deletion limits are described under Retention. To refuse future transfers, stop using the hosted service and request account deletion; hosted sign-in, synchronization and AI connections then become unavailable. Provider information: Supabase privacy and contact information.

Cloudflare Inc. — United States company; global processing network — network and proxy

Network request information, including IP addresses, and MCP requests and replies pass through Cloudflare when you visit this site or use the MCP connection, to deliver and protect the service. Network and security records are retained under the provider's operational retention settings; application content follows the account retention described above. To refuse future proxy transfers, do not use the MCP connection; AI tool access through it becomes unavailable. Provider information: Cloudflare privacy and contact information.

The AI provider you connect — user-chosen provider and processing countries — planning

Requested saved plans, results, interests, notes, retained originals and selected calendar titles and times are transferred when your approved connection calls a tool, to provide planning and the changes you request. Provider retention and processing countries depend on the AI service you choose and its settings. Review its privacy and contact information before approving the connection. You can refuse by not connecting, withholding product permissions or disconnecting; this prevents future tool access but does not remove information already received by the AI provider.

Apple and Google — sign-in

Sign-in identifiers and identity tokens are exchanged with Apple or Google and Supabase Auth when you choose that sign-in method, to authenticate your account. Their processing countries and retention depend on their services. Provider information: Apple privacy information and Google privacy information.

Cloudflare Inc. and Google LLC — support and privacy email — the United States and other countries where these providers operate data centers

Your email address, message, attachments you choose to include and correspondence metadata are transferred when you email support@one-by.one or privacy@one-by.one. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards them to Google (Gmail) to deliver, store and respond to your request. Provider contacts: Cloudflare privacy and contact information and Google privacy and contact information. Please use the in-app deletion and consent controls if you do not wish to send an email.

Apple — United States and other locations described by Apple — App Store purchases

Purchase and transaction information, app-account association and verification requests are exchanged when you purchase, restore or verify a subscription, to process purchases and confirm access. Apple determines processing locations and retains its purchase records under its policies; one-by.one retains linked subscription metadata to verify access while the account exists. Apple may send further purchase notifications after account deletion. Unlinked purchase notifications are handled under the short retention period described below. You can decline purchases and cancel renewal through Apple; paid access may be unavailable, while existing-data reading and account deletion remain available. Provider information: Apple privacy and contact information.

Our production server is in the United States. Cloudflare's network, Apple, Google, the email provider and the AI provider you choose may process data in the United States or other countries outside your residence. Foreign laws may permit access by public authorities. Choosing a feature does not waive protections required by the law that applies to you.

International processing differs by feature. Hosted account processing, MCP disclosure to an approved AI service, opening a prompt link, and support email are separate data flows. For each flow, the notice identifies the recipient, data, purpose, destination countries, transfer timing and method, retention and how to decline.

## Advertising and tracking

We do not sell personal data or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising within the meaning of applicable US state privacy laws. We do not use personal data for targeted advertising or track users across other companies' apps or websites. Authorized disclosures to service providers and the AI you choose are described above; each AI connection requires its own approval.

## Retention

Account content is retained while the account exists. Corrections and withdrawals of activity interpretations can preserve originals and history; they are not privacy deletion requests. Confirmed account deletion removes account-owned content from the live database, subject to the limited records below.

- Deletion receipts expire 30 days after creation. Expired receipts are removed when the deletion-cleanup job runs.

- Apple revocation jobs become eligible for deletion once they are more than 30 days old and no retained deletion receipt references them. Encrypted authorization material is cleared when revocation processing completes; unsuccessful jobs can retain it until cleanup.

- Unlinked Apple purchase notifications expire seven days after receipt and become eligible for cleanup. Expired notifications are not used to link purchases.

- Subscription-claim IP-hash records with a rate-limit window older than one day are deleted when a subsequent claim request runs the cleanup. This is not a guaranteed 24-hour deletion deadline.

- Bug reports become eligible for cleanup after 180 days and account-linked reports are deleted earlier with the account.

- Calendar snapshots become eligible for cleanup after their shared window has been over for more than one day.

- AI write receipts have a 24-hour replay window; device write receipts have a seven-day replay window. Expired receipts can remain while needed for pending corrections or active synchronization.

- Waitlist entries become eligible for cleanup 30 days after the launch notice, or when unsubscribed. Waitlist IP-hash rate-limit records become eligible after two days of inactivity.

Expiry or cleanup eligibility is not the same as completed deletion.

## Deletion and disconnection

To delete your account in the app, open the menu, tap Delete account below Sign out and confirm. If you cannot reach the account menu, including during setup, email privacy@one-by.one for deletion assistance.

When the server confirms account deletion, the sign-in account and its account-owned plans, results, interests, memories, calendar snapshot, connections, device records and bug reports are removed from the live database. There is no account-restoration grace period. Limited deletion receipts, Apple revocation jobs, independent rate-limit records and later unlinked Apple purchase notifications can remain for the purposes and periods described under Retention.

After server confirmation, the app removes this account’s local records, session, device credentials and notifications from this iPhone. A failed local cleanup requires a retry. Account deletion does not cancel an Apple subscription or automatically erase AI chats, support email, shared images, exported files, other-device copies or operating-system backups.

Apple authorization revocation is attempted where applicable.

Manage independently held copies through the relevant provider, or contact us for help.

The current app creates no private CloudKit backup. If earlier app data appears in iCloud, manage it in iOS Settings › Apple Account › iCloud › Manage Storage. Account deletion does not remove separate CloudKit copies or synchronizing backup keys; deleting iCloud app data does not establish that those keys are removed.

Disconnecting an AI app revokes future tool access. It does not erase records or copies that app already received.

## Children

one-by.one is for people aged 16 and older. We do not offer accounts for children under 16. If you believe an account belongs to someone under 16, contact privacy@one-by.one so we can investigate and arrange the required deletion.

## Policy changes

We may update this policy. Updates will appear here with a revised effective date.

## Common privacy rights and request procedure

Everyone can use this request procedure. The statutory rights, exceptions and remedies that apply depend on your location and the law covering our processing; the regional items below add to this common procedure and are not an exhaustive list of applicable local protections.

Email privacy@one-by.one to request confirmation of processing, access, correction, deletion, a portable copy, consent withdrawal, restriction or objection to processing. Identify your account, country or US state, and the information and action involved so we can apply the relevant rights. These requests are separate from ordinary activity corrections in the app, which may retain originals.

The current app can share day and week summaries as images. It does not currently provide an in-app download of all account records. To request a portable copy, email privacy@one-by.one. We will verify the request and explain the available format and the response period that applies.

We may ask for the minimum information needed to verify your identity and authority. Do not send passwords, sign-in tokens or identity documents unless we explain a necessary, secure verification method. Where applicable law allows an authorized agent, the agent can use the same contact; we may ask for proof of authorization. We do not discriminate against you for exercising a privacy right, though a feature may no longer work without the data or consent it needs.

We respond within the period required by the law that applies to your request and explain any extension, refusal or exception. If you disagree, reply to privacy@one-by.one with an appeal or complaint; we will explain the outcome and any further review route available under applicable law. You can also complain to the regulator described below.

## Major regional privacy rights

## United States — state privacy laws and health data

Where applicable state law covers our processing, you may confirm processing, access, correct, delete or obtain a portable copy of personal data, withdraw consent, and object to or opt out of certain processing, including sale, advertising-related sharing, targeted advertising or qualifying profiling. We do not sell data, share it for cross-context behavioral advertising or use it for targeted advertising. California residents have applicable rights to know the categories and specific pieces collected and disclosed, and to limit qualifying uses of sensitive personal information. The collection categories, sources, purposes, recipients and retention are described in this policy; sensitive information is used for the requested features. You may use an authorized agent where permitted and appeal a refusal where state law provides that right. You can contact your state Attorney General or, in California, the California Privacy Protection Agency.

Washington consumer health data: where the My Health My Data Act applies, you may confirm whether we collect, share or sell your consumer health data; access that data, including a list of third parties and affiliates with whom it has been shared or sold and contact information for them; withdraw consent to collection and sharing; and request deletion. We do not sell it. A covered deletion request also requires us to notify relevant affiliates, processors, contractors and other third parties with whom we shared it, as required by the Act. You may appeal a refusal through privacy@one-by.one and, after an appeal is denied, complain to the Washington State Attorney General. These rights apply to covered consumers, including people whose health data is collected in Washington.

Nevada consumer health data: where SB 370 applies, you may confirm collection, sharing or sale, review or obtain a copy of your consumer health data, request the required list of third-party recipients, withdraw consent to collection and sharing, and request deletion. We do not sell it. You can appeal a refusal through privacy@one-by.one and contact the Nevada Attorney General about concerns.

## Canada, including Quebec

Under PIPEDA and applicable provincial law, you may request access and correction, withdraw consent subject to legal or contractual restrictions and reasonable notice, and challenge our handling of your data. Sensitive information, including health-related data, requires express consent. Quebec's Law 25 also provides applicable rights to request cessation of dissemination or de-indexing in specified circumstances and to obtain computerized personal information collected from you in a structured, commonly used technological format, subject to legal exceptions. Contact our privacy officer first, or complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada or the applicable provincial regulator, including Quebec's Commission d'accès à l'information. Seungeun Kim is the person responsible for the protection of personal information, including for Quebec, at privacy@one-by.one.

## Australia

Under the Privacy Act and Australian Privacy Principles, where applicable, you may request access and correction and complain about our handling of your data, including overseas disclosures. Sensitive information, including health information, is collected with explicit consent unless a legal exception applies. You can withdraw optional consent or request deletion through the contact above; access, correction and complaint rights do not create a general statutory right to erasure. If your complaint is unresolved, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner.

## New Zealand

Under the Privacy Act 2020, you may request access and correction and, if a correction is not made, request that a statement of correction be attached. IPP 12 governs applicable disclosures outside New Zealand. You can withdraw optional consent or request deletion through the contact above, subject to applicable retention requirements, and complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner.

## Singapore

Under the PDPA, where applicable, you may request access and correction and withdraw consent with reasonable notice. We explain the likely consequences of withdrawal and stop the affected collection, use or disclosure unless the PDPA or another law permits or requires it. Overseas transfers must meet the Transfer Limitation Obligation. Contact our Data Protection Officer using the details below; you may also complain to the Personal Data Protection Commission. Requests for deletion or a portable copy are handled through our request process, subject to applicable law.

## Brazil — LGPD

Where the LGPD applies, you may request confirmation and access, correction, anonymization, blocking or deletion of unnecessary, excessive or unlawfully processed data, and portability subject to applicable rules. You may request information about recipients, refusal of consent and its consequences, withdraw consent, and request deletion of consent-based data subject to legal retention exceptions. You may also request review of decisions based solely on automated processing that affect your interests and information about the relevant criteria. Contact Seungeun Kim at privacy@one-by.one; you may petition Brazil's National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) or applicable consumer protection bodies. Sensitive health data and international transfers require the grounds and safeguards applicable under the LGPD.

## Republic of Korea — PIPA

salad76, a sole proprietorship in the Republic of Korea represented by Seungeun Kim, doing business as one-by.one, is the personal information controller. The following PIPA notice applies to our processing as a Korean operator, together with the detailed sections above.

- Purposes and data: the purposes and consent section and collection list describe account sign-in, plans and results, synchronization, approved AI access, subscription verification, security, support and the launch waitlist. Saving and syncing records requires storage consent; each AI connection and calendar sharing are separate, optional choices.

- Retention and destruction: account content and limited residual records follow the expiry and cleanup criteria in Retention and the limits in Deletion and disconnection. Expiry or cleanup eligibility is not the same as completed deletion.

- Third-party provision: when you approve an AI connection and its permissions, OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude) or another provider you choose receives the requested plans, results, memories, retained originals and selected calendar data for your requested planning and changes. Each AI connection requires its own approval. That provider retains its independently received copies under its own policy and settings. Declining or withdrawing approval prevents the corresponding future AI tool access. Disclosures required by law are limited to the applicable legal basis; we do not sell personal data or disclose it for targeted advertising.

- Entrusted processing: Supabase Inc. provides hosted account authentication, database storage and server processing; Cloudflare Inc. provides website delivery, security, the MCP proxy and Email Routing; Google LLC (Gmail) provides support and privacy mailbox storage and delivery. Entrusted tasks are limited to the service purposes described above. Apple and Google sign-in, Apple purchases and independently chosen AI services also involve those providers' own processing under their policies; their role must be distinguished from processing solely on our behalf.

- Overseas transfers: International processing differs by feature. Hosted account processing, MCP disclosure to an approved AI service, opening a prompt link, and support email are separate data flows. For each flow, the notice identifies the recipient, data, purpose, destination countries, transfer timing and method, retention and how to decline. See the international-transfer notice.

- Privacy officer: Seungeun Kim, privacy@one-by.one; postal address: 302, 173 Donggwang-ro, Seocho-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea. This is also the contact for privacy complaints.

- Exercising rights: you or an authorized representative may email privacy@one-by.one to request access, correction or deletion, suspension of processing or withdrawal of consent, and applicable explanations or review of qualifying automated decisions, subject to PIPA's exceptions. Use the common request procedure; we verify only the information necessary and explain any legal refusal. You may seek help from the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC), the Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee or KISA's privacy complaint center.

## Japan — APPI

Where APPI applies, you may request disclosure of retained personal data and applicable third-party provision records, correction, addition or deletion of inaccurate data, and cessation of use, erasure or cessation of third-party provision where the statutory conditions are met. Health information can be special care-required personal information; we obtain the consent required for its collection and provision unless a legal exception applies. Foreign transfers require applicable information and consent or another permitted basis; entrusted overseas processing is not automatically exempt. Contact privacy@one-by.one using the common procedure or raise concerns with Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC).

## India — DPDP

India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and implementing rules have a phased commencement. Where the relevant provisions are in force and apply to our processing, Data Principals may request information about processing and sharing, correction, completion, updating and erasure, withdraw consent, seek grievance redressal and nominate another person to exercise rights in the circumstances the Act permits. Use privacy@one-by.one for requests or grievances; after using the required grievance process, you may use the Data Protection Board of India's complaint route when available under applicable law. Cross-border processing remains subject to applicable government restrictions. Where the DPDP children's-data provisions apply, processing data of users under 18 requires the applicable verifiable parental consent and child-data safeguards. Our general minimum age of 16 does not waive those requirements.

## Connect instructions for AI agents
Machine-readable copy: https://one-by.one/connect/index.md. Human pages: https://one-by.one/connect/ and https://one-by.one/ko/connect/. Commands were checked against each tool's official documentation on October 5, 2026; menus can vary by version.

Server URL: https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp. Transport: remote streamable HTTP. Authentication: OAuth sign-in in the browser with dynamic client registration; local loopback redirects are allowed; no API key, token or client secret. Suggested server name: onebyone. Permissions: context:read, activity:read, activity:write. Limit: 3 AI connections per account. Clients that are not verified appear as Unverified app on the approval screen. Do not ask the user for a token. Merge the entry into existing settings. Do not create or change plans until the user asks.

Instruction a user can paste into an agent:
```text
Add the one-by.one MCP server to yourself and connect it.

- Server URL: https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp
- Transport: remote streamable HTTP. Name the server "onebyone".
- Auth: OAuth sign-in with dynamic client registration. There is no API key or token, so do not ask me for one.

Steps:
1. Add the server to your MCP configuration and keep my existing servers. If you cannot change your own configuration, give me the exact command or setting for this client.
2. Start the OAuth sign-in. If you cannot open a browser, show me the sign-in link.
3. I will sign in to my one-by.one account and approve the permissions: context:read, activity:read and activity:write. The approval screen may label you "Unverified app"; that is normal for unverified clients.
4. When I am back, confirm that the onebyone tools are listed. Do not create or change any plans until I ask. If the connection is refused because the limit of 3 AI connections is reached, tell me.

Instructions for each client: https://one-by.one/connect/index.md
```

Per-tool commands (name onebyone, source = official documentation):
- Claude Code (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp): `claude mcp add --transport http onebyone https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp`; then run `/mcp` inside a session and authenticate.
- Codex CLI (https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp): `codex mcp add onebyone --url https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp` then `codex mcp login onebyone`. TOML alternative in ~/.codex/config.toml: [mcp_servers.onebyone] with url = "https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp".
- Cursor (https://cursor.com/docs/mcp): in .cursor/mcp.json or ~/.cursor/mcp.json, {"mcpServers": {"onebyone": {"url": "https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp"}}}. Save, restart, complete OAuth.
- VS Code with GitHub Copilot (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration): in .vscode/mcp.json, {"servers": {"onebyone": {"type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp"}}}. Start the server in the editor and sign in.
- Gemini CLI (https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/mcp-server/): in ~/.gemini/settings.json or .gemini/settings.json, {"mcpServers": {"onebyone": {"httpUrl": "https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp"}}}; then run `/mcp auth onebyone` inside a Gemini CLI session.
- Windsurf / Cascade (https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/mcp): Cascade "..." Actions > MCPs > Open MCP config file; in mcp_config.json, {"mcpServers": {"onebyone": {"serverUrl": "https://mcp.one-by.one/mcp"}}}. The official guide covers the legacy Cascade agent.
- ChatGPT (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/connect-chatgpt): enable Developer mode if the account allows it, open Plugins, select +, name it one-by.one, enter the server URL, finish the OAuth sign-in, then select it in a new chat. Availability depends on plan and workspace policy.
- Claude web and Desktop (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp): Customize > Connectors > add a custom web connector, name it one-by.one, paste the server URL, choose sign-in authentication and automatic client registration if shown, complete OAuth, then enable it in the conversation.

Mandatory consumer protections in the user's country or state of residence and the right to bring a claim in the courts of the user's country under those protections are preserved.

Support: support@one-by.one. Privacy and deletion help: privacy@one-by.one. To request in-app account deletion, open the menu and tap Delete account below Sign out, then confirm. Support has no promised response time for ordinary requests. Privacy-rights requests are handled within periods required by applicable law.

To disconnect an AI, tap Disconnect in the iPhone app under Settings › AI apps, use Disconnect on its one-by.one authorization page, or remove the connector through the AI service’s controls. Revocation blocks future tool calls but does not delete records or copies the AI has already received.
